title: Create compact core token set for embedded widgets and dense UIs
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Summary:
Create a compact variant of Redwood's core design tokens to support embedded widgets and dense data surfaces (small charts, table rows, alert banners inside third-party apps). This work introduces a namespaced compact token set (e.g. token-compact/*) that maps to existing tokens via aliases, updates the type scale for small contexts, tightens spacing and radius tokens, and flattens shadow/elevation for low-profile surfaces.

Problem / motivation:
Embedded widgets often render within host UIs with constrained vertical space. Using the default token set causes visual bloat and inconsistent alignment with host apps. We need a formally supported compact token set so product teams can opt into denser layouts without bespoke overrides. This also reduces the number of one-off component overrides engineers maintain.

Scope (what's in):
- Define compact variants for color palette keys (secondary/neutral emphasis), compact type scale (small/label/body-sm), condensed spacing tokens (gap-2..gap-8), smaller radii tokens (radius-sm/radius-xs), and reduced elevation tokens (shadow-sm/none).
- Add token aliases so components can opt-in via a theme flag (theme: compact).
- Update core components used in embedded flows: Button (compact size), Table row density option, Chart axes label sizes, Form inputs (compact density).

Out of scope:
- Global restyling of all Redwood Console screens. Default theme remains unchanged.

Expected impact:
- Reduce vertical height of embedded widgets by ~18-28% depending on component composition.
- Consistent appearance across hosted/dedicated/private deployments when using embedded SDKs.
- Easier product adoption of compact footprint for partners and customers embedding Redwood widgets.
acceptance_criteria: A1: A namespaced compact token set exists in the tokens repo and is importable (tokens/compact/*).
A2: Components can be rendered with theme=compact and match Figma compact specs for spacing, type, and elevation.
A3: Accessibility: color contrast for compact palette adheres to WCAG AA for body text (>=4.5:1) and large text (>=3:1) where applicable.
A4: Storybook shows component variants (default vs compact) with visual diff snapshots; visual regressions documented.
A5: Migration notes and a short migration guide are published in Confluence and linked from the tokens package README.
design_notes:
Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/Redwood/compact-tokens-2025
Design approach: create a minimal set of overrides instead of duplicating the entire token graph. Use aliasing so tokens/compact/<token-name> resolves to tokens/core/<token-name> when not overridden.
Accessibility notes: when reducing spacing and type scale, prioritize color contrast and hit target sizes for interactive controls (min 32px tap target where possible). For table rows where tap targets are smaller, add explicit documentation for keyboard focus rings.
Handoff: export tokens JSON from Figma and place in tokens repo under packages/tokens/compact. Provide token diff against core tokens for the release notes.
decisions: D1: Introduce 'compact' namespace rather than changing core tokens to avoid regressions in default theme.
D2: Compact type scale will use a -1 step for small bodies (e.g., body-sm = body - 1 step) rather than custom font sizes per component.
D3: Elevation will be reduced to two nominal levels in compact (none, low); drop 'medium' and 'high' shadows from compact set.
D4: Buttons expose a compact size prop that maps to existing button variants; no new button component created.
D5: Color emphasis reduction: maintain primary contrast but reduce secondary/tertiary saturation in compact to avoid visual weight in dense layouts.
implementation_plan:
1) Create token spec document and compact token mapping in Figma (owner: Ava).
2) Export JSON and open tokens repo PR that adds packages/tokens/compact and aliasing logic (owner: Liam, ENG review).
3) Update design-system package to consume compact tokens behind a 'compact' theme flag; add Storybook examples and visual tests (owner: Sima Rao).
4) Update components used in embedded widgets (Button, Table, Charts, Form controls) to accept density prop and use themed tokens.
5) QA cycle: automated visual diff + manual QA on smallest supported screens and embedded host backgrounds.
6) Publish migration guide and announcement; provide rollout plan for partner teams to opt in.
7) Post-release: monitor adoption and surface any accessibility regressions; revert or tweak tokens if significant issues found.
links: Embedding SDK doc where compact will be referenced: https://docs.redwood.ai/embedding-sdk#density-themes
comments: 2025-02-10 Ava Chen: Created ticket after sync with product; initial research shows ~20% height savings on a sample alerts+chart widget when using compact spacing and smaller axes labels.

2025-02-12 Liam Patel: Did a quick feasibility review with runtime engineers. Alias approach looks straightforward; will need to add a small runtime guard in the tokens loader to prefer compact namespace when theme flag present.

2025-02-18 PM feedback (Maya Gupta): Please ensure any compact color changes are reviewed by security/compliance if they affect log visuals in regulated workflows. Adding 'security_review_required' but setting to false pending further review.

2025-02-21 Sima Rao (Engineering Design): Prototype components updated in the playground; shared Storybook link in the Figma file comments for visibility. Noted that table row density required a small API tweak to expose padding token mapping.
2025-02-27 Liam Patel: Opened draft PR in tokens repo adding compact mapping and export script. CI failing on snapshot tests — working with QA to update baselines for compact stories only.
2025-03-03 Ava Chen: Design review done with PM and front-end leads. Agreed to keep default theme untouched and ship compact as opt-in. Added acceptance criteria for WCAG checks.
2025-03-05 QA (Jordan Kim): Visual diffs look stable for Button and Form fields; charts need axis label spacing tweak (in-flight). Leaving note for Sima to adjust axis label token mapping.
